objective.en: Detect active wildfire cells quickly enough to support community evacuation planning.

sources.name: NASA FIRMS VIIRS 375 m active fire detections, Suomi NPP and NOAA-20 (via NASA GIBS)
sources.usage: Fire cells and their first-detection day come from VIIRS 375 m thermal anomaly detections, 7-13 Jan 2025 (Palisades, Eaton, Hurst and Kenneth fires). The mission runs 8-13 Jan UTC (day 0 = 8 Jan); cells already burning on 7 Jan start on day 0. Persistent industrial heat sources are masked with a Nov 2024 baseline. Smoke/cloud blocking and sensor detectability are modelled.

objective.en: Map flooded neighborhoods through cloud cover and deliver actionable coverage within 12 hours.

sources.name: NASA GPM IMERG and OPERA DSWx (reference datasets)
sources.usage: Flood and cloud patterns are educational models inspired by precipitation and surface-water products; cells are not current observations. The MODIS flood product for Hurricane Beryl (Jul 2024) was checked but is almost entirely cloud-obscured, so it is not used.

objective.en: Identify the hottest urban areas with sufficient accuracy to prioritize heat-response resources.

sources.name: NASA MODIS Aqua 8-day daytime land-surface temperature (via NASA GIBS)
sources.usage: Heat cells are the hottest 40% of populated cells by observed daytime land-surface temperature, 11-18 Jul 2024. Cloud blocking and sensor detectability are modelled.

sources.name: NASA SEDAC Gridded Population of the World v4, 2020 density (via NASA GIBS)
sources.usage: Cells with at least 500 people per square kilometre count as populated neighbourhoods.
